meta.title: PulseMind — ICU breathing-risk prototype
meta.description: A student research prototype that brings ICU readings for patients on ventilators into one view, ranked by estimated breathing risk.

home.eyebrow: DECISION SUPPORT SOFTWARE FOR INTENSIVE CARE
home.headline: Which patient needs you first?
home.subline: A clearer view of breathing risk across patients on ventilators.
home.status: Student research prototype · Sample data · Not in clinical use

problem.title: Patient information is spread across several screens.
problem.body: In a busy intensive care unit (ICU), checking on a patient on a ventilator — a machine that helps them breathe — can mean looking at several separate screens and records. That makes a slow decline in breathing harder to notice.
problem.heroLabel: types of information source each clinician uses, on average, to review a patient's breathing

bars.label: Blood gas and lab results (blood tests)

problem.closing: The data already exists — it's just scattered.
problem.source: Survey of 36 ICU clinicians (22 nurses, 14 doctors) at Nhân dân 115 and Nam Sài Gòn hospitals, [MONTH YEAR]. More than one answer allowed. An early local picture, not a national one.

approach.title: One clear picture, ranked by who may need review first.
approach.leadIn: A read-only view that turns scattered bedside data into one clear picture of breathing risk — to help clinicians decide which patient to review first.
approach.audience: Built for ICU doctors and nurses caring for adults on ventilators.

diagram.caption: How PulseMind is designed to connect

steps.title: Brings the data together.
steps.text: Collects each patient's readings from different sources in one place.

steps.title: Estimates who may be at risk — and shows why.
steps.text: Estimates how likely a breathing problem is soon, and shows the readings behind it in plain language.

steps.title: Highlights who may need review.
steps.text: Flags a patient when risk gets high enough — not an alert on everything.

approach.honesty: Every estimate also says how complete and how recent its data is. When the data is too thin, PulseMind says so instead of showing a number.
approach.readOnly: PulseMind only points and explains. It never diagnoses, treats or touches a device. Every decision stays with the clinician.
approach.closing: 28 of the 36 clinicians we surveyed said a tool like this would be useful — if it is proven safe and fits how they work.

demo.title: See the prototype for yourself.
demo.intro: The demo runs on simulated patients, so you can click through it freely. It shows three screens: the whole unit at a glance, one patient in detail, and the history of a single reading.

progress.title: A working prototype — and an honest next step.
progress.anchor: PulseMind is a working prototype, not a finished product. Here's what we've done and what comes next.

done.title: Clinician survey · Nhân dân 115 Hospital
done.text: 22 ICU doctors and nurses told us how they review patients on ventilators.

done.title: Prototype built
done.text: Built on public ICU data from over 36,000 patients, to show how the idea could work.

done.title: Second survey · Nam Sài Gòn Hospital
done.text: A second ICU team shared their workflow, taking the total to 36 clinicians.

now.title: Prototype
now.text: Built on public ICU data. Shows how the concept could work; it is not yet clinically validated.

ahead.title: Agree and test
ahead.text: Decide with doctors what PulseMind predicts and how far ahead, then test it on past hospital data.

ahead.title: Connect
ahead.text: Connect to real ICU equipment and collect approved data from a Vietnamese hospital.

ahead.title: Trial safely
ahead.text: Test PulseMind alongside normal care without affecting clinical decisions, to check it is accurate and safe — then begin a supervised, read-only trial.

progress.closing: Read-only at every step — clinicians stay in charge.

notProven.title: What we have not proven
notProven.text: That PulseMind improves care, saves time, or notices a patient's decline earlier. Those are exactly the questions the next stages exist to answer.

team.title: Six students, one question.
team.intro: We are a student team from Ho Chi Minh City University of Technology (HCMUT — Bách Khoa), working across data, software, design and business.
team.clinicalInput: With clinical input from Dr Mai Hữu Xuân and Dr Tuấn — guidance, not hospital approval.

contact.title: Help us test the idea properly.
contact.intro: PulseMind only becomes useful if it is shaped with the people who would use it. Here is where you can help.

cards.title: Hospitals
cards.body: We are looking for an intensive-care partner: a hospital with an adult ICU, patients on ventilators, and records we may study — so we can agree what to predict and test PulseMind against what actually happened.
cards.subject: [Partnership] PulseMind

cards.title: ICU doctors and nurses
cards.body: Try the demo and tell us what is missing, confusing or wrong. Clinician feedback has shaped every version so far.
cards.subject: [Feedback] PulseMind demo

cards.title: Researchers and mentors
cards.body: We have open questions on labels, validation and prediction timing, and welcome advice from people who have done this before.
